column12: why 0.1212 and not the filed-stage rate: Summit's Q2 2026 10-Q (0001599298-26-000068) states 'The FDA noted that a statistically significant OS benefit is necessary to support marketing authorization in this setting, and the PFS results from this study may not be sufficient to support marketing authorization.' The prespecified primary OS analysis missed (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.62 to 1.01, p=0.057), and the later cuts (HR 0.78, nominal p=0.0332, September 2025; HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.61 to 0.95, nominal p=0.0151, June 2026; 8-K 0001599298-26-000081) are not alpha-controlled. An approval needs the FDA to accept less than the bar it stated, and the nearest published rate is approval within a year after the FDA's advisers voted the evidence short. Oncology NDA/BLA to approval, 92.0%, assumes no such statement and is not used. The case for higher: the western subgroup's OS hazard ratio moved from 0.98 to 0.76 with follow-up and the FDA has that cut, and Summit says no approved regimen in this setting has shown a significant OS benefit. The case for lower: an advisory vote is advice, while this is the agency's own stated position, and 273 of HARMONi's 438 patients were Asian (8-K 0001599298-26-000081). The weights move with either line's build, so recompute the blend and both legs when they do
